title: Silver
Feels Worse

post.title: Why Second Place Feels Worse Than Third #shorts
post.description: Which are you: silver or bronze? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who calls second place 'losing.' Dev won silver at the 5K and he's sulking, while Theo, in third, can't stop grinning. In 'When Less Is More: Counterfactual Thinking and Satisfaction Among Olympic Medalists' (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1995), Victoria Husted Medvec, Scott Madey and Thomas Gilovich had people rate TV footage of medalists at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics on a scale from agony to ecstasy. Bronze medalists looked happier than silver medalists, both right after the event and on the podium. Their explanation: silver compares up ('I almost won gold'), bronze compares down ('at least I got a medal'). Psychologists call these 'what might have been' thoughts counterfactual thinking. Later research suggests it also depends on what each athlete expected, so it isn't a law of nature, but it explains why 'almost' can sting more than 'not quite'. #psychology #shorts #olympics #mindset #overthinking
